walkthroughs.body_html:
Ethical Legal Cultural Issues — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ethical Legal Cultural Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ethical Legal Cultural Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: The most recently added (top) - LIFO.
Any item, randomly.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
The first one added (FIFO).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
Any item, randomly.
They are the same gate with different names.
OR is true when at least one input is true; XOR is true when exactly one input is true.

mcqs.q: What is the time complexity of binary search?
options: O(n) - because it searches through items.
O(1) - because it is fast.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.
O(log n).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Flowchart”?
options: Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
